text:
maya: Heads up — after the FP8 canary (rwd-fp8-v2) we see ~12% p99 tail increase on long-ctx workloads vs the INT8 baseline. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/8342

sam: Saw that too. Is KV hit rate the same? Any changes to kernel selector recently?

maya: KV hit ~0.985 (unchanged). Flame graphs point to spikes in KernelSelector::select() and host-device memcpy around KV lookup for layers ~20-24. Quick excerpt:

```
Flame samples:
KernelSelector::select       34%
FP8Kernel::run               26%
memcpy (host->device)        18%
KVCache::read                12%
Other                        10%
```

jules: Hmm. Could be layout/packing causing extra copies for FP8 path. We did touch packing in PR #4123 — maybe packing now does an extra staging buffer for some layer sizes. Also, did we accidentally include lm_head in the FP8 mask? Canary config should exclude embedding/lm_head.

indra: Microbench confirms: for layers with large KV (seq_len > 2048) FP8 kernel throughput drops ~20% vs INT8. Likely extra dequant/depack on fast path. Repro: `./bench --model rwd-ggml-long --seq 4096 --batch 1 --layer 22 --kernel fp8` -> 280ms vs int8 230ms. PR #4123 modified packing thresholds.

ciara: Can we push a quick mitigation? Proposal: apply a per-layer mask to exclude last-6 transformer layers + lm_head from FP8 canary, and force INT8 for layers where routing sees seq_len > 2048. Also temporarily tighten batching window. I can open a hotfix PR.

maya: Do it. Also change batching heuristics: when avg_seq_len > 1024 reduce continuous batching window from 10ms -> 3ms (to avoid huge prefixes accumulating).

deploy-bot: Canary update: rwd-fp8-v2 scaled 3 -> 6 replicas (canary) by @ciara.

perf-bot: Synthetic perf run (longctx job) with layer_mask mitigation shows p99 delta down to +4% vs baseline. job: perf/longctx/fp8/2026-03-18

sam: Good. We should also rerun calibration; current calibration set is short-context heavy and might bias quant stats. Rerun with mixed-length prompt set. cc @ciara

jules: Also a product idea: kernel selector cost model should include kv_size_in_bytes and memcpy cost estimate. Right now we just model FLOPS and weight size. I can prototype a KV-aware selector that favors INT8 when kv_bytes > X.

ciara: Hotfix PR created: #4178 — adds layer_mask (exclude last 6 layers + lm_head), routing rule for seq_len > 2048 -> int8, and batching window tweak. Includes unit tests and a perf-run link.

maya: Thanks. Action items: 1) rerun full bench with top-100 prompts for calibration, 2) add kprobe to record host-device memcpy sizes in the hot path, 3) prototype kv-aware kernel selection cost model.

indra: I'll add microkernel probes for memcpy sizes and measure aligned vs unaligned copies. Assigning kernel-selector prototype to @jules.

jules: Noted. I'll sketch cost function: cost = alpha*FLOPS_est + beta*memcpy_bytes/PCIe_bw + gamma*depack_overhead(layer_type). Need perf constants.

maya: We're keeping revert criteria: if canary p99 > +7% for 6 consecutive perf runs we'll revert to int8. For now monitor dashboard and perf-bot jobs. :thumbsup:

ciara: Added monitoring alert: perf::longctx::p99_delta > 7% for 6 runs -> pager for eng-runtime oncall.

sam: One more note — check whether the packing change introduced extra GPU scratch allocation per-batch which reduces SM occupancy for large sequence sizes. If so, occupancy drop could explain throughput regression.

maya: Good catch. Please log any occupancy regressions in the bench runs.

ciara: PR #4178 is merged to canary. Running post-merge perf suite now. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/8349

perf-bot: post-merge suite complete: p99 delta = +3.6% (long-ctx), avg latency +1.1%. Next run scheduled in 30m.

maya: Great. We'll reconvene if anything crosses the revert threshold. Thanks all.
